neighbours.label: a past-tense life-story step: 'moved to <place>' or 'decided to …' after an opening clause that sets the occasion
fire: After graduating in 1888, Clara moved to Chicago, where she worked as a nurse.
Beaten in the election, he moved to Virginia to practise law.
When the mill closed, the family moved to Detroit to look for work.
Widowed at thirty, she moved to Dublin and opened a boarding house.
Tired of waiting, she decided to walk home through the fields.
After the fire, the brothers decided to rebuild the barn in stone.
In 1910 the young painter moved to Paris, where he met his future wife.
Refused a loan, he decided to sell the horses and start again.
quiet: A graduate of 1888, Clara lives in Chicago, where she works as a nurse.
Beaten in the election, he was bitter about Virginia for years.
The mill is closed, and the family lives in Detroit without work.
A widow at thirty, she runs a boarding house in Dublin.
The walk home through the fields is long and tiring.
The barn of the brothers is built in stone.
The young painter loves Paris, where his future wife was born.
His horses are for sale, and the loan is still unpaid.

notes: Weak pole (max 3.42) with a 41% gate-closed regime. Probes: 'moved to Boston' 0.67, 'decided to sell' 0.31, 'returned to Ohio' 0.28, 'emigrated to' 0.08, present-tense versions 0.07-0.09. Only 'moved' and 'decided' are supported, so the test uses those two.
